sentence: A 25-year-old Colombian patient was admitted to our Obstetrics Section due to rupture of membranes during 24 weeks and 5 days of pregnancy.
She did not report any family or personal history of interest.
Gynecological history: menarche at age 14; FM: 3-4/32.
In a routine pregnancy examination performed at 20 weeks of gestation, she was diagnosed with vaginal condylomatosis.
Upon inspection of the external genitalia, multiple vulvoperineal condylomas were observed.
TV: cervix formed, posterior and closed.
Ultrasound: fetus in longitudinal cephalic view.

Treatment with intravenous antibiotics was started and a series of complementary tests were performed (complete analysis with PCR, serology; vaginal and rectal cultures and amniotic fluid; and hybridization test for HPV), the results of which are reflected in Table 1, and which allowed us to reach the diagnosis of chorioamnionitis.
Delivery was triggered a week later and due to the presence of chorioamnionitis and fetal immaturity, it was allowed to progress.
The delivery was spontaneous, with a live male fetus weighing 690 g, artery pH 7.24 and vein pH 7.48.
Placenta of 167 g, hypermature with signs of chorioamnionitis.
After delivery, biopsies of the vagina and perineum were performed, the results of which were: condyloma acuminatum of the vagina and condyloma acuminatum of the perineum that respected the edges.
The newborn died at 40 days of life.
